chunks: The obligations of Hajj are seven: ihram, and the four talbiyat,
and they are: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika laka labbayk'

Other than that of the talbiya is sunnah. It is recommended for the one uttering talbiya to frequently say: 'Labbayk dha al-ma'arij labbayk', for that is the talbiya of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family).

The tawaf around the House is an obligation. The two units of prayer at the maqam of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is an obligation. The sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa is an obligation. The standing at 'Arafa is an obligation. The standing at al-Mash'ar is an obligation. The hady al-tamattu' is an obligation. And whatever else from the rites of Hajj is sunnah.

key_terms.تلبية: Talbiya — the ritual invocation 'Labbayk' uttered during ihram as a response to God's call to pilgrimage
key_terms.سنة: Sunnah — recommended practice that does not carry the obligatory weight of fard
key_terms.فرائض: Obligatory acts (singular: farida/fard) — acts whose performance is required and whose omission invalidates or requires atonement
key_terms.هدي التمتع: Hady al-tamattu' — the sacrificial animal required for those performing the combined Hajj al-tamattu'

ai.seo_question: What are the seven obligatory acts (fara'id) of Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, from the assembly of Sheikh al-Saduq held on Friday the 13th of Sha'ban 368 AH, enumerates the seven obligatory acts (fara'id) of Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence. The text carefully distinguishes between fard (obligatory) acts — ihram, four-part talbiya, tawaf, prayer at Maqam Ibrahim, sa'i, wuquf at 'Arafa and Mash'ar, and hady al-tamattu' — and sunnah (recommended) acts. Notably, the specific talbiya 'Labbayk dha al-ma'arij' is highlighted as the Prophet's own practice.
